body:
[aida:advisor] REWORK RELAY FOR #1974 (STORY-1350/1357), not your sweep. Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED at eb35c424f36d4ebcc6798662b2564b1c551135cd.

FIRST, THE GOOD PART, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE PRIOR VERDICT DID NOT: BOTH BINDING ROUND-3 REQUIREMENTS ARE SATISFIED AND CLOSED.

    R1  marker constant + coupling test - IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER at lib.rs:77000,
        extract_implementer_approach reads it, and pickup_template_and_reader_share_one_marker
        include_str!s the MASTER template and asserts it contains the constant. The reviewer
        confirmed BOTH directions fail: edit the template heading, red; edit the constant, red.
        Reading the master rather than the scaffolded copy was the right call.
    R2  absence note + end-to-end test - append_implementer_approach emits "_None recorded._",
        and the new test drives the REAL generator through a temp store asserting both arms.
        That is the seam the helper-only tests could not see, tested at the seam.

ONE NEW FINDING, AND IT IS THIS COMMIT'S OWN SUBJECT. I VERIFIED IT IN THE TREE AT YOUR HEAD RATHER THAN RELAYING IT:

    lib.rs:77000   pub(crate) const IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER: &str = "## Implementer approach";
    lib.rs:~77015  (first_line.trim_end() == IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER)          <- correct
    lib.rs:~77032  "...did not leave a comment beginning `## Implementer approach`, so this
                    review has no stated intent to check the diff against."        <- LITERAL

The absence message hard-codes the marker as a literal, thirty-two lines below the constant introduced to stop exactly that. Three production sites now name the marker - the constant, the template, the message - and the coupling test covers only constant-to-template.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE DEFECT IT REPLACES, which is the reviewer's argument and I think it is right. Rename the constant tomorrow: the parser follows it; the template is caught by your new test and forces the edit; AND THE MESSAGE STILL TELLS THE HUMAN TO WRITE THE OLD HEADING. The system then parses for X while instructing reviewers to write Y. The original defect had both sides agreeing and silently not matching. This one has them DISAGREEING IN THE INSTRUCTIONS - the state where a human follows the prompt and is wrong. Your own constant's doc comment says the failure is invisible "precisely because both sides still work"; this adds a third side with no test at all.

REMEDY AS THE SEAM, NOT AS THE SITE: no production string names the marker except the constant. A `format!` with `{IMPLEMENTER_APPROACH_MARKER}` is the whole fix. Do NOT extend the coupling test to grep the message - make it structurally impossible, which is what the constant is for. That is binding.

EXPLICITLY NOT A FINDING, and the reviewer checked rather than pattern-matching on "the string appears again": the test-file literals at story_1350_review_approach_tests.rs:11, 14, 26 and 95. Those are FIXTURES, and a fixture that builds its input from the constant cannot detect a change to the constant. Literal is correct there. Do not "fix" them.

MERGE STATE, separate predicate: Build (ubuntu-latest) pending at eb35c424f36d and the merge-hold label is present by design. Not mergeable either way.

PROCESS NOTE YOU SHOULD HAVE: the reviewer could not read the round-3 requirements from the handshake file at all - a drain-recorded verdict had been clobbered and its summary said only "both binding requirements remain missing" without naming them. They recovered the content from the GitHub comment at 2026-09-20T23:18 and then quoted both in full in this verdict so nobody repeats the archaeology. That is BUG-1539's third instance and the first with a measured recovery cost; it is on the spec. If a prior round's requirements are ever unreadable to you, the GitHub review comment is the durable copy - and say so rather than guessing.
subject: REWORK RELAY #1974: both binding round-3 requirements SATISFIED - one new finding, the absence message hard-codes the marker the commit exists to couple (verified in your tree); remedy is the seam, a format! with the constant
